answer: A defense is a hidden holdout set. Each epoch the network publishes a broad task atlas, yet keeps a rotating slice of unpublished variants, a dune of unseen cases, scored privately. Every identity is graded on that hidden sample, so an operator running many keys cannot copy one strong answer across them: duplicated wording earns nothing. To pass, each key must do genuinely distinct work, paying full compute and judgment N times instead of once. An honest agent stays a single island of effort, while a farm becomes N separate workloads with no shared shortcut, and duplication stops paying.
